final_message:
The Case of the Vanishing Water Heater

Last Tuesday morning I went down cellar for a jar of peaches and found the floor an inch deep in water. It wasn't a flood, exactly, but it was enough to set a person's heart going, and I stood on the bottom step a good while trying to decide whether to go on or back up.

Mr. Stewart was sent for. He was out in the barn, where he had been all morning doing something to a harness, and he came in a little slowly, as a man does who suspects he is wanted for trouble. He looked at the floor. He looked at the water heater. Then he said, "Weel, that's a fine mess," which is what he says about everything from a broken plate to a hailstorm, so it didn't help much.

We found the trouble soon enough. A small pipe at the back of the heater had worked loose and was dripping steadily, and had been doing so, as near as we could figure, since Sunday. The drain in the floor was stopped up with an old wash rag that nobody would own to. Of course, the dog was blamed first, but he was asleep on the porch and looked so innocent that it seemed hardly fair.

Mr. Stewart went to get a wrench, and I went to get the mop. We met again at the head of the stairs, each of us carrying the wrong thing. He had the mop and I had the wrench. We stood and looked at each other, and I think neither of us could have said which one laughed first.

It took the best part of the morning to set matters right. I carried out the pails, and he lay on his back behind the heater with a lantern in his teeth, saying things in Scotch that I am glad the neighbors couldn't hear. When at last the pipe was tight, he came out wet to the elbows and announced that he had known all along it was that very pipe. "Then why," I asked, "did ye not say so on Sunday?" He pretended not to hear.

The peaches, I am happy to say, were on the top shelf and came to no harm. We had them for dinner, and I must say they were the best we have put up in years. I think it was the cellar water that did it, though I wouldn't tell Mr. Stewart so.
